construction: always-on, short 1x perp + long 1x spot, equal notional both legs, 50/50 BTC/ETH; inception=first day, exit=last day

waterfall_detail.comment: layer 'plus_rebalance' alone removes 4.07 SR (>2): the sleeve's edge is thin relative to this friction.
layer 'plus_margin_cost' alone removes 3.41 SR (>2): the sleeve's edge is thin relative to this friction.

0.0 by construction: compute_price_pnl marks the spot-perp basis to market every day via spot_ret - perp_ret on actual price series, so entry/exit basis convergence is already in the hedge P&L. Charging a separate boundary-basis layer would double-count.

notes: Turnover 'per side' interpreted as one execution (open OR close) touching both legs: spot(taker+spread) + perp(taker+spread) = 0.0016; inception charges one open, final exit one close. Rebalance charges the full round-trip cost (2x open = 0.0032) on the drift notional per the brief. Drift tracked by compounding each leg's equity with its own daily return since the last rebalance (long spot +spot_ret, SHORT perp -perp_ret) and resetting to target on rebalance. AMBIGUITY RESOLVED: modelling the short-perp leg with +perp_ret makes it track spot so |drift| never reaches 20% and rebalance count is 0 (degenerate); -perp_ret is the drift-generating reading, since a short's equity falls as the perp rises. Margin cost is a constant daily rf drag on 1/3 of perp notional (leverage<=3x). Boundary-basis layer recorded as 0.0 (already marked-to-market).
